structured.rankingRationale: Top priority goes to events with explicit lodging mechanisms and exact dates, while committed competitor venues are deliberately ranked as future-capture/overflow rather than open inventory. Campus and downtown events without a published block remain targeted verification opportunities because the 157-room hotel can plausibly serve delegates, speakers, side meetings or receptions but no demand volume is assumed.

notesForDeepResearch: Verify organizer and housing/PCO contacts for every retained candidate.
Prioritize TMEC, FMF200, Toronto Breast Imaging, SMDM, CAG and CSRS for open sourcing and speaker/overflow lodging checks.
For committed competitor venues, test future-edition rotation and overflow only with evidence.
materialUncertainties: No published peak-room or room-block counts were found for the retained candidates.
Several current editions are committed to competing hotels; they are future-capture/overflow signals, not open inventory.
Public sources did not establish a future Toronto wedding or family-reunion programme with a named organizer and exact date in the reviewed set.
Hotel restaurant/lounge operating status remains unverified.

result.text: Structured discovery of 13 future Toronto event-related opportunities from 2026-12-07 through mid-2028, with exact dates, venues, sourcing posture, hotel fit, uncertainty, and next research actions. Current competitor-hosted events are labeled as venue-confirmed and treated as future-capture/overflow signals rather than open inventory.
